## Braintree Data Migration

Braintree's collected import guide documents a managed route for moving customer and payment-method data from another processor into a Braintree gateway. The merchant first requests an export from the current or former processor and asks that processor to transfer it securely; Braintree's preferred flow uses PGP keys, encrypted SFTP credentials, files encrypted with Braintree's public key, and a Braintree-performed import. [[source-braintree-get-started-data-migration-imports]]

## Import boundaries

The guide limits a migration to a bulk import plus one follow-up import for customers created during the processing switch, and it excludes periodic imports for backup or failover. After import, Braintree says it returns a logfile of created customer IDs and payment-method tokens. Supplied mapping identifiers should be checked against existing Vault customers to prevent collisions.

The page covers credit cards, PayPal Billing Agreements, Apple Pay, Google Pay and US ACH, with method-specific inputs and conditions in the raw source. The PayPal Business Account used for imported billing agreements must match the account linked to the Braintree gateway. Imported Apple Pay and Google Pay methods do not guarantee successful transactions because final acceptance remains with the cardholder's bank or issuer. Treat the snapshot as collected evidence rather than proof of current import availability or processor participation. [[source-braintree-get-started-data-migration-imports]]
